title: REPORT on the control of the financial activities of the European Investment Bank Group – annual report 2024
part_text: 15. Recalls that any allocation of funds by the EIB, through InvestEU and other financial instruments for defence purposes and for investments in critical technologies, must fully respect the national security interests of the Member States and comply with the principles of the EU and international law, most notably the do no significant harm (DNSH) principle; underlines that the competent audit authorities and bodies of the EU institutions should deliver thorough and continuous audit controls to third entities and third countries that are beneficiaries of EU funding and that deliver investments and projects in the defence field, to ensure the transparent use of EU funding; stresses that the outcome of such investments and projects must not undermine the national security, economic and social interests of the Member States, nor the interests of recipients and non-recipient third countries; calls on the EIB to expand its focus on enhancing regional resilience in the areas of energy, employment, housing, education and climate; emphasises the important role that the EIB can play in the creation of publicly-owned infrastructure that supports regional development and fosters greater economic cooperation between Member States;
